newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court upholds Pallas Stern liquidation.
newsitem.headline: French court upholds Pallas Stern liquidation.

text.p: The Paris Court of Appeal on Friday upheld a decision to liquidate bank Pallas Stern made by the commercial court in February, court sources said on Friday.
The ruling opens the way to persue former managers or supervisory members, who are accused of being responsible for the biggest French banking bankruptcy in half a century.
Pallas Stern will close with liabilities of 13.5 billion francs against assets of 5.7 billion.
The liquidation decision is in line with the wishes of many of the creditors who preferred an immediate liquidation over pay-back plans that would have lasted some 20 years.
There are also some 15,000 bond holders of Pallas Stern.
